title: Messaging, Queues & Event Streaming
summary: Design asynchronous communication with explicit delivery, ordering, replay, schema and backpressure semantics.

modules.title: Asynchronous communication foundations
modules.summary: Understand why moving work across a message boundary changes correctness and failure semantics.
modules.why: A queue is not just a faster thread handoff; it introduces durable state, duplicate delivery and independent failure.

units.title: Synchronous vs asynchronous boundaries
units.summary: Choose async communication based on latency, coupling and failure isolation.
units.challenge: Redesign a slow email/report request path into async work and define the new user-visible states.
units.evidence: Before/after sequence diagrams and failure-mode comparison.

units.title: Message envelopes & contracts
units.summary: Define enough metadata to trace, deduplicate and evolve messages.
units.challenge: Define an event envelope for a multi-tenant activity system.
units.evidence: Schema plus rules for IDs, timestamps and compatibility.

units.title: Broker queues vs distributed logs
units.summary: Distinguish transient work distribution from retained replayable event history.
units.challenge: Choose RabbitMQ-style queue or Kafka-style log for six workloads.
units.evidence: Decision matrix with replay, ordering and retention requirements.

modules.title: Queue brokers, routing & work distribution
modules.summary: Use queues and exchanges/topics to distribute work across consumers safely.
modules.why: Routing and acknowledgement choices determine load distribution and loss/duplicate behaviour.

units.title: Work queues & competing consumers
units.summary: Scale worker throughput while preserving per-message ownership.
units.challenge: Scale an email worker pool and observe distribution under uneven processing times.
units.evidence: Throughput/queue-depth measurements.

units.title: Routing, fan-out & topic patterns
units.summary: Deliver messages to one or many logical subscribers using routing rules.
units.challenge: Route task events to notifications, audit and analytics consumers without application-side branching.
units.evidence: Broker topology diagram and routing tests.

units.title: Broker durability & high availability
units.summary: Understand what durable queues/messages do and do not guarantee across broker failure.
units.challenge: Kill broker/consumer processes at different points and document surviving/lost/duplicated outcomes.
units.evidence: Failure matrix and configuration recommendation.

modules.title: Delivery semantics & idempotent consumers
modules.summary: Make message processing correct under loss, crash and duplicate delivery.
modules.why: At-least-once delivery is common; business side effects must survive repeated execution.

units.title: At-most-once & at-least-once processing
units.summary: Trace where acknowledgment timing creates loss or duplicates.
units.challenge: Crash a consumer before/after side effect and demonstrate both loss/duplicate possibilities.
units.evidence: Processing timeline with chosen ack strategy.

units.title: Idempotent consumers & deduplication
units.summary: Turn repeated messages into one logical side effect.
units.challenge: Process duplicate payment/notification-like events safely across concurrent consumers.
units.evidence: Concurrency tests proving one business outcome.

units.title: Exactly-once claims & transactional boundaries
units.summary: Understand where exactly-once is achievable and where external side effects break the abstraction.
units.challenge: Analyze an 'exactly once' design that writes DB and sends email; identify the remaining duplicate window.
units.evidence: Boundary analysis distinguishing transport guarantee from business guarantee.

modules.title: Retries, dead letters & poison messages
modules.summary: Recover transient work without infinite retry storms or silent data loss.
modules.why: Retry queues are operational control systems and can amplify outages if unbounded.

units.title: Message retry policy & delayed retry
units.summary: Separate immediate retry from scheduled redelivery with bounded attempts.
units.challenge: Design retries for an external notification provider outage without hammering the provider.
units.evidence: Retry schedule and capacity calculation.

units.title: Dead-letter queues & operator recovery
units.summary: Make terminal failures visible, diagnosable and replayable.
units.challenge: Create a DLQ workflow with diagnosis, fix and safe selective replay.
units.evidence: Runbook and replay controls.

units.title: Retry storms & failure amplification
units.summary: Prevent queues from turning downstream incidents into prolonged overload.
units.challenge: Model outage/recovery where a huge backlog releases at once and protect the dependency.
units.evidence: Recovery throughput plan and backlog-drain policy.

modules.title: Kafka distributed-log architecture
modules.summary: Understand partitions, replicas, offsets and retention as the basis of event streaming.
modules.why: Kafka semantics make more sense when treated as a replicated ordered log, not a magic queue.

units.title: Topics, partitions & offsets
units.summary: Understand ordering and parallelism within a partitioned log.
units.challenge: Choose keys/partition count for project activity events and observe ordering.
units.evidence: Partition strategy with throughput/order trade-offs.

units.title: Partition leaders, replicas & durability
units.summary: Understand producer durability and broker failure at partition level.
units.challenge: Compare producer acknowledgement settings under broker loss.
units.evidence: Durability/availability table by configuration.

units.title: Retention & log compaction
units.summary: Use time/size retention and latest-value compaction for different event/state needs.
units.challenge: Design topics for audit events vs latest account-state changelog.
units.evidence: Topic policy definitions and consumer implications.

modules.title: Kafka consumers, groups & rebalancing
modules.summary: Scale consumers while understanding ownership movement, lag and duplicate windows.
modules.why: Consumer-group dynamics are a common source of latency spikes and duplicate processing.

units.title: Consumer groups & partition ownership
units.summary: Understand how partitions distribute across group members.
units.challenge: Scale consumers above/below partition count and observe assignment.
units.evidence: Assignment diagrams and throughput observations.

units.title: Offset commits & processing correctness
units.summary: Place offset commits relative to side effects deliberately.
units.challenge: Crash processing around commit and side effect boundaries.
units.evidence: Failure timeline and chosen commit protocol.

units.title: Rebalancing, lag & slow consumers
units.summary: Operate groups under deploys, skew and slow processing.
units.challenge: Create partition skew and a slow consumer, then design alerts/scaling/remediation.
units.evidence: Lag dashboard definition and operational playbook.

modules.title: Event schemas & compatibility
modules.summary: Evolve shared events without breaking replay or independent consumers.
modules.why: Events persist longer than services; historical records must remain interpretable.

units.title: Event schema & semantic design
units.summary: Publish stable facts rather than internal entity dumps.
units.challenge: Redesign a 'TaskUpdated' blob event into stable domain facts.
units.evidence: Event catalog with ownership/semantics.

units.title: Backward/forward/full compatibility
units.summary: Understand reader/writer compatibility across event versions.
units.challenge: Evolve an event through producer/consumer rollout combinations.
units.evidence: Compatibility matrix and test cases.

units.title: Replay across schema evolution
units.summary: Keep historical replay possible after business models change.
units.challenge: Rebuild a projection from three historical event versions.
units.evidence: Replay strategy and translation tests.

modules.title: Transactional outbox, CDC & integration events
modules.summary: Publish database state changes without unsafe database+broker dual writes.
modules.why: Dual writing to independent systems creates an unavoidable partial-failure window without coordination.

units.title: Dual-write failure problem
units.summary: Understand why DB commit + broker publish cannot be assumed atomic.
units.challenge: Enumerate every failure point in DB-write-then-publish and publish-then-DB-write designs.
units.evidence: Failure matrix demonstrating inconsistency windows.

units.title: Transactional outbox pattern
units.summary: Commit business state and publication intent atomically in one database.
units.challenge: Implement outbox publication with crash/restart and duplicate-safe consumers.
units.evidence: Integration tests forcing failure at commit/publish/ack boundaries.

units.title: Change Data Capture & event propagation
units.summary: Stream database logs/changes into downstream systems while preserving ownership semantics.
units.challenge: Design DB-to-search/analytics CDC and decide where domain semantics are introduced.
units.evidence: CDC architecture with failure/rebuild plan.

modules.title: Stream processing & stateful event computation
modules.summary: Compute continuously over ordered/unordered event streams with time and state semantics.
modules.why: Real-time aggregates require explicit handling of event time, late data and recovery.

units.title: Transforms, joins & state stores
units.summary: Build stateful stream topologies and understand repartitioning.
units.challenge: Build real-time project activity counts and join member metadata.
units.evidence: Topology diagram and partition/state explanation.

units.title: Event time, windows & late data
units.summary: Separate event occurrence from processing arrival time.
units.challenge: Compute 5-minute metrics with deliberately delayed/out-of-order events.
units.evidence: Expected/observed results under late-data policies.

units.title: State recovery & processing guarantees
units.summary: Recover stateful processors consistently after failure.
units.challenge: Restart a stateful processor and prove aggregate correctness after replay.
units.evidence: Recovery test and guarantee boundary analysis.

modules.title: Event-driven architecture patterns
modules.summary: Use events to decouple capabilities without losing ownership, traceability or comprehensibility.
modules.why: Event-driven systems can reduce temporal coupling while creating hidden dependency graphs.

units.title: Events, commands & ownership
units.summary: Distinguish a fact that happened from an instruction requesting work.
units.challenge: Classify a set of cross-service messages and fix ambiguous ownership.
units.evidence: Message catalog with producer/consumer responsibilities.

units.title: Choreography vs orchestration
units.summary: Choose decentralized reaction or explicit workflow coordination.
units.challenge: Design onboarding/payment-like workflow both ways and compare change/failure complexity.
units.evidence: Two sequence diagrams plus decision record.

units.title: Event sourcing & CQRS
units.summary: Understand when immutable event history and separate read models justify complexity.
units.challenge: Prototype event-sourced task state and projection, then identify reasons not to use it by default.
units.evidence: Prototype plus cost/benefit ADR.

modules.title: Backpressure, lag & async capacity
modules.summary: Keep producers, brokers and consumers stable when rates differ.
modules.why: Async systems hide overload temporarily; unbounded backlog converts latency problems into storage/outage problems.

units.title: Queue depth, backlog age & service rate
units.summary: Model producer/consumer rate imbalance quantitatively.
units.challenge: Calculate and validate how long a worker fleet takes to drain an outage backlog.
units.evidence: Capacity model compared to measured drain time.

units.title: Backpressure & admission control across async boundaries
units.summary: Signal or enforce capacity rather than accepting infinite work.
units.challenge: Protect an async export service from an unlimited producer burst.
units.evidence: Admission policy and overload test results.

units.title: Observability for queues & streams
units.summary: Measure end-to-end event health, not just broker uptime.
units.challenge: Define dashboards/alerts for a message pipeline and inject a slow consumer.
units.evidence: Monitoring spec with symptom-based alert thresholds.
